---
title: Running and adapting a template
---

## Run a notebook locally {#from-a-template-to-a-run}

Download a notebook from the [template catalog](templates.qmd). Open it in your
project’s Python environment, edit its **parameters** cell, and run the cells in
order. The example inputs are copied into your project when you run the notebook.
For your own study, supply the input files and give each run its own output folder.

## Run in Colab

Use **Open in Colab** on a template page, then save your own copy before editing.
The [Colab setup guide](colab-setup.qmd) explains running cells, using your own
files and keeping outputs between sessions.

Keep the template’s short installation cell and input-preparation call. The cell
installs JAXCMR from GitHub’s `main` branch; input preparation copies selected
examples from that installation. Update the installation when you need newer
library code or examples. Custom input files remain yours to provide. Colab labels
the first raw cell “Unsupported Cell Type”; it contains website metadata and is
skipped during execution.

## Choose a working directory {#paths-and-working-directories}

The `project_root` parameter selects the base for **all** relative input and output paths:

| Setting or execution context | Base directory |
|---|---|
| An explicit `project_root` | That directory; a relative value uses the kernel's starting directory. |
| Local checkout, `project_root=None` | The enclosing Git root, found by the existing `find_project_root()` helper. |
| Standalone folder, `project_root=None` | The kernel's working directory. |
| Colab, `project_root=None` | The runtime's working directory. |

Running from `templates/` or a nested
prepared-job directory inside a checkout uses the same project inputs and outputs.
When the kernel starts outside the project, supply `project_root` explicitly. The
root belongs to your research project; it is not the installed JAXCMR package directory.

Absolute paths remain absolute, and `~` expands to your home directory. On Windows,
`"C:/Users/Alex/my-study"` or `r"C:\Users\Alex\my-study"` works; avoid a partially
specified drive path such as `"C:my-study"`. UNC paths are supported on Windows.
Relative defaults such as `"data/Dupertuys2026.h5"` work on both platforms. An absolute
path from another computer must be updated there.

The input helper copies recognized relative example names into this same base on every platform. Custom files
remain your responsibility; selecting an absolute custom path does not download an
example over it. Path resolution happens after parameter injection and does not
change the process's working directory.

## Reuse fits and simulated responses {#saved-products-and-regeneration}

Pass the fit JSON paths displayed by fitting to simulation, then supply the printed
`simulation_paths` to model comparison or their values as analysis `data_paths`.
The defaults continue to use the supplied examples until you replace them. For example,
a one-model simulation job can use:

```python
fit_paths = {"CMR": "results/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo_best_of_3.json"}
```

`output_dir` supplies default locations, but explicit directory settings take precedence:

| Procedure | Directory precedence |
|---|---|
| Fitting | New JSON records go under `output_dir/fits` or the explicit `fit_dir`. Inspection reads `saved_fit_paths`. |
| Simulation | Explicit `simulation_dir` and `figure_dir` override `output_dir`. The example sets `simulation_dir="results/simulations"`. |
| Parameter shifting, model comparison and analyses | Explicit `figure_dir` overrides its default; summary tables use `output_dir`. |

Give independent jobs distinct names or directories for every product they write.
Choose `fit_action="inspect"` to read named records, or `"estimate"` to run the optimizer. To resume batch jobs, `"fit_if_missing"` estimates a model only when its destination file is missing. Give changed models or selections new destinations. Simulation can reuse matching responses with `redo_sims=False`. An empty `figure_str` displays plots without saving them.

The fitting notebook recalculates the objective at the saved parameters so you
can compare it with the recorded value. If you edit data or model code in place,
give the run a new output location or regenerate the affected fits and simulations.

You can also supply settings externally. [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/parameters.html)
and [Papermill](https://papermill.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage-parameterize.html)
use the same tagged cell. An override replaces a whole top-level value: to
change one model, supply the complete `model_configs` dictionary for that work unit.
Use `fit_alg_path` and `fit_hyperparams` to select and configure the optimizer. Analysis
templates accept a list of response files (`data_paths`) and a matching list of
names (`data_labels`). Each trial query applies to every file.

## Adapting a procedure

Adapt the settings cell: input paths, trial selection, parameters
and output folder. Check the meanings of item codes, participant identifiers,
categories and response padding before interpreting results. Retain the same
selection for comparisons that are intended to address the same observations.

Use one-entry lists for a single file or trial selection. Set
`comparison="datasets"` to compare response files within each condition, or
`comparison="conditions"` to overlay selections from one file. The dataset label
titles a condition overlay and the condition labels identify its curves. In the
category SPC template, `comparison="categories"` overlays item categories
within each condition. Each figure is saved separately. A run that produces
one figure uses the supplied `figure_str` as its filename stem.

Additional research notebooks, with their own input requirements, are available in the
[repository’s templates directory](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr/tree/main/templates).

### Comparing observed and simulated SPCs {#spc-model-inputs}

In the bundled Dupertuys example, the `list_type` field codes mixed lists as 1,
pure emotional lists as 2, and pure neutral lists as 3. The [SPC notebook](templates/spc.ipynb)
starts with observed recall for each of those conditions. To overlay model
predictions, supply the simulated response files alongside the observations.
These settings include all three bundled models. For one model, keep its entry
and the observed entry in both lists.

```python
data_paths = [
    "data/Dupertuys2026.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad_demo_best_of_3.h5",
]
data_labels = ["Observed", "CMR", "Source-only eCMR", "Broader eCMR"]
comparison = "datasets"
```

## Execute a report with Quarto

With [Quarto installed](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/), you can execute a
notebook with overrides and render its results to HTML. Python parameter injection uses Papermill, which the repository's default `uv sync`
already installs. For this example, run from the repository root and select the
environment for Quarto using the command for your shell:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS / Linux

```bash
export QUARTO_PYTHON="$(uv run python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)')"
```

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
$env:QUARTO_PYTHON = (uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)")
```

:::

Save the settings for the third recall in `pnr-third.yml`:

```yaml
output_positions: [2]
output_dir: results/pnr-third
```

Run the notebook with these settings on either platform:

```text
quarto render templates/pnr.ipynb --execute --execute-params pnr-third.yml --output pnr-third.html
```

Quarto normally executes from the notebook's directory; the template's root lookup
handles that. An injected `project_root` also works for notebooks prepared outside
the project. The website build does not execute notebooks.

Output positions are zero-based, so `[2]` selects the third response.
The explicit `--execute` runs the notebook; rendering an `.ipynb` without it
normally displays its stored results. The website displays saved example outputs.

## Prepare independent jobs with Papermill

For a cluster batch, it can be useful to inspect the complete set of jobs
before executing any of them. Papermill's `prepare_only=True` creates a
configured notebook for each job. From the repository root, the following Python cell prepares two
fitting runs that differ only in optimization seed and output folder:

```{python}
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Prepare two fitting jobs without running them"

from pathlib import Path
from copy import deepcopy
import nbformat
import papermill as pm

source = nbformat.read("templates/fitting.ipynb", as_version=4)
defaults = {}
parameter_cell = next(cell for cell in source.cells
                      if "parameters" in cell.metadata.get("tags", []))
# Evaluate only the parameter assignments, not the fitting procedure.
exec(parameter_cell.source, defaults)

jobs = Path("analyses/rendered")
jobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for seed in [0, 1]:
    configs = deepcopy(defaults["model_configs"])
    for config in configs.values():
        config["seed"] = seed
    path = jobs / f"fitting_seed_{seed}.ipynb"
    prepared = pm.execute_notebook(
        "templates/fitting.ipynb", str(path),
        parameters={"fit_action": "estimate", "model_configs": configs, "output_dir": f"results/fitting-seed-{seed}"},
        prepare_only=True,
    )
    # Stored example results are not results from this new job.
    for cell in prepared.cells:
        if cell.cell_type == "code":
            cell.outputs = []
            cell.execution_count = None
    nbformat.write(prepared, path)
```

To prepare one model per job, pass a one-entry `model_configs` dictionary. Preserve the
project's chosen job boundaries: a model collection does not require running every model in
each scheduled job. Inspect the injected settings in each notebook. Execute one from the working
folder with:

```text
uv run papermill analyses/rendered/fitting_seed_0.ipynb analyses/rendered/fitting_seed_0.ipynb --cwd .
```

The same prepared notebooks can be transferred with their inputs and run as
separate Slurm jobs, using the project folder as the working directory. This
keeps the prepared paths portable: set `--cwd` to the destination project folder, or
inject its `project_root` when executing. Do not inject a local machine's absolute root
into jobs intended for a different machine. This matches the [remote-cluster workflow](https://github.com/githubpsyche/sbatch/blob/master/workshop/04-prepare-work-units.qmd):
maintain a procedure, prepare concrete work units, then schedule their execution.
Preparing jobs does not fit a model; rendering HTML is a separate presentation step.

For participant jobs, the fitting template uses `pooled=False` and
`subject_indices=[i]`, where `i` indexes the sorted participant IDs. Simulation
and parameter exploration can instead vary seeds or parameter values. Choose
the work unit around the scientific question and keep its inputs and outputs
explicit. Fitting ends at the JSON record. Pass that file to the simulation template to generate responses.
